sanskrit_verse: तस्याम् एव तु यो भुक्तौ ब्राह्मणो रमते रसात् । काण्डपृष्ठश् च्युतो मार्गाद् अङ्कितोऽयं प्रकीर्तितः ॥
transliteration: tasyām eva tu yo bhuktau brāhmaṇo ramate rasāt | kāṇḍapṛṣṭhaś cyuto mārgād aṅkito 'yaṃ prakīrtitaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: He who, being a Brāhmaṇa, indulges in sensory enjoyment during the period of Vedic study, having fallen from the path of discipline, is thus marked and declared unfit.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from adherence to Dharma, not birth alone
Causation through conscious choice and volitional deviation
Capacity-based responsibility tied to spiritual station and vow
Restoration logic requiring realignment with svadharma
Consciousness alignment as determinant of eligibility
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent.birth_category = 'Brāhmaṇa' AND agent.vow_status = 'active' AND agent.sensory_indulgence = 'true' THEN eligibility_for_ritual_functions = 'revoked'
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that Brāhmaṇas under vow bear heightened responsibility. Deviation results in automatic suspension of ritual and societal authority until completion of prescribed reintegration. The court must verify both the act of deviation and the status of the vow at the time.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is direct observation of conduct violating svadharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how sensory indulgence disrupts sequential spiritual progression. Responsibility is proportional to vow-bound capacity. The marking serves not punishment but realignment, preserving Dharma's integrity without inflicting suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate svadhyaya completion protocol to restore focus
Assign guru-guided pratikriya for sensory recalibration
Reintegrate through supervised ritual service before full eligibility
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law is established: Dharma flows from consciousness, not caste by birth alone. Restoration supersedes punishment. Reality aligns with Dharma when consciousness is sovereign.
